items.title: David Finck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 29, 2015
items.q: I say to myself there’s no way. I could never play that Wagner tone poem.

ctx.x: I was reading and a word popped out that’s been written about you is ubiquitous. Like you’re all over the place I guess. And I wondered if you made a conscious career choice between classical and jazz. Could you have gone either way?

Well I would say that I started out as a classical bass student at the Eastman School of Music, which is a pretty well-known conservatory. I was good enough to get in. I think they only took four or five of us at a time. Now when I look at the guys, my friends who play in the Metropolitan Opera Orchestra or the New York Philharmonic, I say to myself there’s no way. I could never play that Wagner tone poem. No way. Because I realize © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

now that I have spent most of my career playing popular music. And it’s a different skill set and it’s another art form. Even though the bass lines function much in the same way. Beethoven’s bass lines are fantastic. And the voice leading is unbelievable. Mozart — it’s the same thing. But you have to spend a lot of time practicing with the bow and learning those parts that are near impossible for me. Those guys breeze through it like it’s a blues. So I don’t know that it was a conscious effort, but I kind of just…
